Tech Scan: AI gateway

This page answers how model and tool calls are routed, guarded and paid for. A gateway sits between the agent and the models and tools it calls, giving the team one place for routing, fallback, keys, budgets and guardrails.

This page is a draft. It covers the AI gateway as a new capability between the harness and context layers: the AWS-first answer, conditional alternatives, research-only notes, what not to use, and the gaps. Entries are research references from web sources reviewed 11–12 November 2026, not locally deployed or benchmarked options.

Read the harness and context sections of Concepts first: Equip the agent and Supply relevant information. The gateway is the control point between them: tools and knowledge reach the agent through it.

On this page
PurposeAWS-first defaultConditional alternativesResearch-only notesDo not useGaps and open questionsSources

Purpose

A gateway sits between the agent and the models and tools it calls. It provides one place for routing, fallback, keys, budgets and guardrails, so those decisions are set once and apply to every call that passes through it. Without a gateway, each agent or client carries its own keys, model choices and fallback behaviour, and the approved-model policy is enforced nowhere in particular.

Readers confuse two different gateways. Tell them apart before choosing one:

  • An LLM router routes model calls across providers. It chooses which model answers, falls back when one fails, and applies one set of keys and budgets to model traffic.
  • A tool/MCP gateway routes tool calls. It exposes approved tools — including MCP servers and knowledge bases — to the agent under policy, and records which tools were called.

This page covers the gateway as a routing and control point. The harness spoke covers the agent loop itself, and the context spoke covers what is retrieved.

Three kinds of traffic pass through a gateway: model calls, tool calls, and retrieval. Model calls go to the approved model through Bedrock. Tool calls go to approved tools and MCP servers through AgentCore Gateway. Retrieval reaches Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases through the Gateway as well, so retrieval shares the same control point as tool calls.

AWS-first default

There is no AWS product that is a multi-provider LLM router. Bedrock is the model API: approved Claude and OpenAI models are reached through Bedrock.[4][5] AgentCore Gateway is a tool/MCP gateway, not an LLM router — do not list Bedrock as a LiteLLM equivalent.

The AWS-first answer is therefore Bedrock plus AgentCore Gateway plus Guardrails plus Policy together.[1][2][3] Each part does one job:

AWS-first gateway components
ComponentWhat it doesWhat it does not do
Amazon BedrockModel API for approved Claude and OpenAI modelsRoute model calls across providers
AgentCore GatewayRoutes approved tool and MCP calls under policyRoute LLM calls across providers
Bedrock GuardrailsContent guardrails on model callsAuthorise tool calls
AgentCore Policy (Cedar)Authorises Gateway tool callsGovern arbitrary shell networking

Know the boundary. Gateway policy governs traffic through the Gateway, not arbitrary shell networking. VPC attachment alone is not evidence of package-only egress or secret denial: outbound enforcement, approved dependencies and credential protection still need their own controls.

The Gateway also fronts retrieval. Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases are exposed through AgentCore Gateway,[6] so the agent reaches them through the same control point as its tools. Begin with Retrieve plus the approved outer model,[7] and approve embeddings and reranking separately.[9] Managed knowledge bases support ACL-aware retrieval,[8] but they do not authenticate the end user — the application must supply verified identity.

Map each control to its actual enforcement point: IAM and resource boundaries; Cedar and AgentCore Policy for Gateway tool authorisation[2]; Guard for structured-data checks[10]; content guardrails; and retained human decisions. Guard checks structured data and Cedar governs configured Gateway requests; neither implies complete policy-framework coverage.

The model policy still applies. Use managed Claude or OpenAI models only, Bedrock preferred; direct provider APIs are exceptions for a specific capability or approved-region gap, after reviewing egress, credentials, retention and data handling.

Conditional alternatives

Use an alternative only when its trigger applies. Each one below is conditional on the situation in its verdict, not a second default.

Apply the hard gates before choosing. A gateway must pass the required-capability, approved data location and retention, identity and authorisation, supported model and API, security boundary and operational-ownership gates first. AWS preference must not override these gates.

Conditional gateway alternatives
ProductLicenceRouting and fallbackSelf-host or managedVerdict
LiteLLM proxyMIT core; enterprise/ paid100+ providers; load balancing, fallbacks, conditional routing; virtual keys and budgetsSelf-host or LiteLLM CloudMulti-provider routing in a VPC. Pin versions: malicious PyPI releases reported March and October 2026.[11]
OpenRouterProprietary managed380+ models; one key; basic routing and fallbackManaged onlyZero-infra start only. Restrict to approved Claude/OpenAI endpoints or do not use. Stripe agreed to acquire it, announced August 2026.[16]
PortkeyMIT core; hosted commercialRouting, fallbacks, load balancing, semantic caching, built-in guardrailsSelf-host or CloudConditional. Palo Alto Networks completed acquisition 29 May 2026 — confirm current terms.[11]
Kong AI GatewayApache-2.0 core; AI features tieredMulti-target failover is Enterprise-onlySelf-host or KonnectOnly if already running Kong/APIM.
Envoy AI Gateway, now Agent RouterApache-2.0Route-level fallback; InferencePoolSelf-host on KubernetesKubernetes-platform-team pick. Renamed 10 September 2026; now an Agentic AI Foundation project.[12]
UnkeyLicence disputed (AGPLv3 vs FSL-1.1-ALv2)Not an LLM router; a key and quota layer beside your codeManaged or self-hostAdd in front of a gateway for third-party key management, never as a substitute.

Apply the decision rule:

  • Zero infrastructure → OpenRouter, restricted to approved models.
  • Full control in a VPC → LiteLLM.
  • Kubernetes-native → Agent Router.
  • Already on Kong → use Kong rather than adding a second gateway.
  • On AWS → Bedrock + AgentCore Gateway + Guardrails + Policy together.

Research-only notes

Langfuse is observability, not a gateway.[13] It connects to gateways for cost data; it does not route model or tool calls. Do not list it as a gateway alternative, and do not expect it to enforce routing, fallback or the approved-model policy.

There is strong public AWS evidence for Langfuse as an observability platform, including official AWS deployment documentation. That evidence supports its observability use, not a gateway use.

Do not use

  • Do not present any gateway as a substitute for the model policy. The policy is managed Claude or OpenAI models only; a gateway does not change which models are approved.
  • Do not route unapproved models through a gateway's fallback. Fallback must stay inside the approved model list — automatic routing must not silently broaden the policy.
  • Do not silently broaden the model policy through managed defaults, automatic routing, fallbacks, retrieval reasoning or evaluator models.
  • Do not list Bedrock as a LiteLLM equivalent. Bedrock is the model API; it is not a multi-provider LLM router.
  • Do not use Unkey as a substitute for a gateway. It is a key and quota layer that sits in front of a gateway, not a router.
  • Do not rely on Gateway policy to control shell networking. It governs traffic through the Gateway only.

Gaps and open questions

  • No AWS multi-provider LLM router exists. A team that needs routing across providers must add a conditional alternative, and carry the model-policy controls that brings.
  • Gateway failover must not silently broaden the approved-model policy. No automatic routing to unapproved models is acceptable as a fallback. Kiro's Auto routing is the cautionary example: current documentation says Auto can route to active models outside the administrator's approved list.[14][15]
  • No option on this page has been locally deployed or benchmarked. Every entry is a research reference from web sources; adoption still needs qualification in the intended account.

Next, record the team's approved-model list and the fallback behaviour it accepts — fail closed, or queue and retry — before adopting any gateway, then read the harness spoke for the managed harness this gateway sits beside.
